implementation_notes: Caliban ships the Relay toolkit for GraphQL services: implement the Cursor trait for a case class plus a Schema so the cursor serializes as an opaque scalar, and expose list fields as connections built from its Connection/Edge/PageInfo abstract classes, with clients paging through first/after. There is no data-layer equivalent, so the resolver still decodes the cursor into a hand-written keyset predicate (Slick, doobie or Quill) ordered by the same unique composite key, fetching first + 1 rows to detect more pages; the Scala-flavoured alternative is streaming those pages lazily as a LazyList or fs2 Stream.
code_sketch:
case class ItemCursor(createdAt: Instant, id: Long)
implicit val cursorSchema: Schema[Any, ItemCursor] = Schema.string   // opaque scalar

case class ItemEdge(cursor: ItemCursor, node: Item)
case class ItemConnection(edges: List[ItemEdge], pageInfo: PageInfo, totalCount: Int)
// resolver: decode `after` -> WHERE (created_at, id) < (?, ?) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT first + 1
pitfalls: The Cursor instance must be schema-exposed as a scalar; otherwise Caliban renders the cursor's internal structure and clients start depending on it, which the opacity requirement exists to prevent.
A base64 cursor carrying filter state must be signed or versioned: an index-based cursor silently returns wrong pages when the filter or sort changes between requests.
